justification: A single serial verify-page run (nothing else running) produced a clean pass: Lighthouse 100/100/100/100 across performance, accessibility, best practices and SEO; 0 console errors; 0 console warnings; 0 broken links (all 17 external sources resolved); mobileOverflowPx 0; report.json failures list is empty (no NEEDS_MARKUS placeholder needed here -- the front matter already carries a real author, so there was nothing pending). This is a materially better shell result than sibling reviews in this batch (cpu-scheduling scored 89 on performance under load); nothing here points at shared shell latency as a concern for this route. Both figures were checked in all four device/theme combinations. Figure 1 (inode/MFT record diagram, viewBox 360x245: a 'file record' box listing size/timestamps/block-list, with a red arrow fanning down to three block boxes 900/901/902) is crisp and fully legible at 390px in both mobile-light-part03 and mobile-dark-part03, and at full width in desktop-light-part02 and desktop-dark-part02 -- no overflow, no clipped labels, correct border/arrow color inversion between themes, caption present with the ext4/NTFS equivalence spelled out. Figure 2 (journal write-ahead sequence diagram, viewBox 360x350: four stacked steps -- write journal entry, write commit record, apply to real location, reclaim journal space -- with two labeled crash-timing arrows) was checked split across mobile-light-part05/06, mobile-dark-part05/06, and whole on desktop-light-part03 and desktop-dark-part03: every step box and both italic crash-annotation labels ('crash before this: nothing to replay' / 'crash after this: journal replays it') are legible at 390px in both themes, with the red-highlighted 'commit record' step correctly inverting to a dark red/pink border in dark mode, and no horizontal scroll on the figure itself in any of the four combinations. Code blocks use the same horizontal-scroll-with-fade pattern as the rest of the site; this was verified as a real rendered fade (not a silent clip) via a pixel-level crop of the flush-stages block's right edge in both themes (mobile-light-part07 crop and mobile-dark-part07 crop both show genuine alpha fade-out on the clipped glyphs, not an abrupt cut). Critically, the content that gets clipped in every code block checked is either a constructor-argument tail (e.g. 'FileMode.Cre...', 'FileShare.Rea...') or a boilerplate temp-path expression -- never the measured value a reader needs. The two OUTPUT panels that matter most (the flush-stages Peek() demo: 'before Flush(): 0 bytes visible...' / 'after Flush(): 20 bytes visible...', and the SaveAtomically demo: '{"retries":3}' / 'temp file still exists: False' / '{"retries":5}') both show their headline numbers before the fold, unlike the cpu-scheduling round's PrintMetrics issue where the cited number was the part hidden. Both exercises collapse correctly: grep across the article source confirms the only two `::::exercise` blocks each contain exactly one nested `:::solution` block with the runnable code and its OUTPUT panel inside the solution, and mobile-light-part06 (exercise 1) and mobile-light-part13 (exercise 2) both screenshot a collapsed 'Show solution' disclosure triangle with zero leaked code or output text above it -- confirming the writer's self-caught fix (moving the final exercise's code/output into the solution) actually landed and rendered correctly. Heading hierarchy is clean: one h1, correct nesting, headings are all content-specific questions rather than boilerplate. Rhythm of prose/code/figure/callout/exercise never runs long without a break across the full 15-part mobile scroll. Illustration depth compares well against the target query's usual top results: GeeksforGeeks' file-systems page and generic OS textbook chapters explain inodes and journaling with static, unlabeled or lightly-labeled diagrams and no runnable verification, where this article's two diagrams are paired with real .NET 10 programs that independently demonstrate the exact claim being illustrated (the Flush() two-stage gap, the atomic rename pattern) -- a bar the comparison sources do not clear. The only nit found, too small to move the score, is that the SaveAtomically code block's `using (var stream = new FileStream(tempPath, FileMode.Create, FileAccess.Write, Fil...` line is clipped even at desktop width (visible in desktop-dark-part07); this is a single very long constructor call, not desktop-specific breakage, and the clipped tail (FileShare.None) is not something the surrounding prose asks the reader to read off the code.
